answer: Requiring every agent identity to be backed by verifiable stake that is slashed on abuse makes mass fake identities expensive: a whisper of reputation only becomes trustworthy when tied to escrowed value. New identities start with a zephyr-thin trust score and must earn standing through completed, attested work before joining high-value trades. A single inlet for onboarding, one verified wallet per identity and rate-limited, stops an attacker spawning thousands of cheap copies, since each clone must pay the same stake and history cost as a real agent.
